finalText:
Five small files, all under `src`, wired together as one request pipeline.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[server.js] -- checks token --> B[auth.js]
  A -- passes user --> C[routes.js]
  C -- reads --> D[cache.js]
  D -- misses go to --> E[store.js]
  C -- writes go to --> E
```

- `server.js` is the front door. It reads the `Authorization` header and rejects anyone `auth.js` can't verify.
- `auth.js` checks bearer tokens shaped like `userId.signature`, signed with an HMAC secret from `AUTH_SECRET`.
- `routes.js` is a small table: `GET /users`, `GET /orders`, `POST /orders`. Reads go through the cache, writes go to the store.
- `cache.js` is a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of reads. No expiry of its own.
- `store.js` is the actual data, in memory, where every record expires 15 minutes after it's last written.

One thing worth knowing before you touch orders: `routes.js` says writes should invalidate the cache, but `POST /orders` never does that. After someone places an order, a cached `orders:<id>` read can stay stale for up to 15 minutes.

Worth a look: `src/routes.js:10`.
